subject: latent state space model weights -- question on example from FAQ #15 and RKR 2010 paper

messages.author: 052dc98fd0a6fd98
messages.subject: latent state space model weights -- question on example from FAQ #15 and RKR 2010 paper
parts:
Hello,

I believe I understand the method by which once can formulate latent state space models. I am not sure, however, of what the weighting factor in the "iid" model is doing when it is set to a negative value. The "iid" documentation does not indicate what negative valued weights do. 

For example in FAQ #15 (http://www.r-inla.org/faq#TOC-I-have-a-complicated-state-space-model-can-this-be-fitted-using-INLA- ) the weight is assigned a value of -2: 

  w = c(rep(NA,n), rep(-2,m)) # weights for j

In the toy example of RKR 2010 (section 4.1 on p.g. 9) the weights (w1) are set to -1. 

Would you please help me understand this or point me to the documentation where I can find out more about these specifications? 

Thanks so very much.

Jae

We can start by
  y_t = x_t + e_t
  x_t = r x_{t-1} + w_t
and them re-write the state equation as
  0 = x_t - r x_{t-1} - w_t
and in this last equation we have weights
  1 for x_t
 -1 for x_{t-1}
 -1 for w_t

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] latent state space model weights -- question on example from FAQ #15 and RKR 2010 paper
parts:
Yes to the first, no to the second. 

When you use the copy mechanism, you can set the scaling parameter as fixed or let it vary. 

Old style:
f(...,copy=..., fixed=FALSE)

New style:
f(...,copy=..., hyper=list(beta=list(fixed=FALSE)))

New style lets you specify the distribution and various other things. 

There's no mechanism to multiply more complicated random effects, so I don't think it's possible to have covariates. 

D

messages.author: f66907f526d3c7bf
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] latent state space model weights -- question on example from FAQ #15 and RKR 2010 paper
parts:
Thanks! And one can simply add more terms, so the code below works.

Alas this is a side project, so I might not get back to it for a couple of weeks. The slides look useful: I also saw mention of marked point processes, which is something else I'll want for another project. I'll have to download them & read through them on my next trip to London.

Bob


set.seed(6996)
NYear1=2000; K1=100; alpha1=0.5; beta1=0.1; sigma1=0.2

x1=numeric(NYear1)
T1=rnorm(NYear1)
x1[1] <- rnorm(1, log(K1), 1)
for(t in 2:NYear1) {
  x1[t] <- log(K1) + (alpha1+beta1*T1[t])*(x1[t-1]-log(K1)) + rnorm(1,0,sigma1)
}
N1 <- rpois(NYear1, exp(x1))

Y1=cbind(c(N1, rep(NA, length(N1)-1)), # data
        rep(c(NA,0), times=c(length(N1), length(N1)-1))) # zeroes for state
Data1=data.frame(Y=Y1,
                t=c(1:length(N1), 2:length(N1)),
                lag1=c(rep(NA,length(N1)), 2:length(N1)-1),
                lag1a=c(rep(NA,length(N1)), 2:length(N1)-1),
                Temp=c(rep(NA,length(N1)), 10*T1[-1]),
                shock=c(rep(NA,length(N1)), 1:(length(N1)-1))
)

# Fit latent model
formula1 = Y ~ f(t, model="iid", fixed=TRUE) + f(lag1, copy="t", hyper=list(beta=list(fixed=FALSE))) + 
                        f(lag1a, Temp, copy="t", hyper=list(beta=list(fixed=FALSE))) +  f(shock, model ="iid")
Gomp1 = inla(formula1, data = Data1,family = c("poisson", "gaussian"),
            control.family = list(list(), list(initial=10, fixed=T)))
summary(Gomp1)$hyperpar

messages.author: f66907f526d3c7bf
messages.subject: Re: latent state space model weights -- question on example from FAQ #15 and RKR 2010 paper
parts:
Oooh, I know the answer to this one. :-)

"Weights" is a horrible term - I'm guessing it made sense originally, its use has been extended. It might be better to think of it as a regression coefficient: in FAQ 15 if you look at the model carefully, you'll see that it becomes

0   = x_t - 2*x_{t-1} + x_{t-2} + v_t,

and the -2 is just the coefficient in front of the x_{t-1}.

Bob
